title: Hejaz Railway
summary: Ordered by Ottoman Sultan Abdulhamid II in 1900 to ease pilgrimage and strengthen Ottoman control of remote provinces, the Hejaz Railway ran south from Damascus through Syria and Jordan and reached Medina in 1908, about 1,300 km. It never reached Mecca. A trip that took about 40 days by camel caravan fell to about 72 hours, and Arab Revolt sabotage from 1916 left it largely unusable.

uncertainty.note: APM: ordered March 1900; Gulf International Forum: construction began September 1900. 1 September 1908 is the "officially opened" date on nabataea.net; APM says the main line "officially reached Medina in 1908".

reviewer_note: Sources conflict: APM says "ordered in March 1900", Gulf International Forum says construction began September 1900; length is "approximately 1,300 km" (APM) while others cited in searches give 1,302 or 1,320 km, and CSMonitor gives about 800 miles; opening 1 September 1908 is from nabataea.net only (APM says only 1908). The 40 days to 72 hours and purpose quote are from The National. Gulf International Forum says 460 km was built by 1904 connecting to Jordan; no stations or dates between Damascus and Medina were confirmed, so waypoints are the two termini. APM, not Wikipedia, supports Arab Revolt sabotage between Ma'an and Medina in 1916. The Medina point is the city centre.

beats.caption: In 1900 Sultan Abdulhamid II orders a railway to run from Damascus toward the holy cities.
The main line officially reaches Medina in 1908, cutting a journey of about 40 days by camel to about 72 hours.
From 1916 Arab Revolt sabotage, especially between Ma'an and Medina, leaves the line largely unusable.
